title: Finite-cover connectedness criterion for abelian étale sections
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and i:Z→X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that for every finite morphism h:X′→X [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and every irreducible closed subset C⊆X′, C∩h⁻¹(range i) is connected and nonempty. Then for every abelian étale sheaf G on X [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], globalSectionsUpperStarMap Ab i G:Γ(X,G)→Γ(Z,i⁻¹G) is an isomorphism, with global sections and inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Lemmas 59.82.4 (09ZG), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZG, and 59.82.2 (09ZF), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZF; underlying abelian sheaf version

proof.text: Apply the Zariski closed-immersion connected-restriction lemma to i, using the identity finite cover and irreducibility of each point closure. For a finite cover h:X′→X, finite morphisms preserve qcqs. Apply the same lemma to pullback.snd i h; Scheme.Pullback.range_snd identifies its image with h inverse image of range i, so the original hypothesis supplies connected point-closure intersections.
Apply gabber_h0_etale_criterion to the two Zariski comparisons and the underlying sheaf of sets of G. This yields bijectivity of the set inverse-image unit at the identity étale object.

Use the inverse-image algebraic-structures theorem to obtain the natural forgetful comparisons and their unit equation. Evaluate that equation at the identity étale object. The two comparison factors are isomorphisms, so cancellation gives an isomorphism for the underlying function of the abelian unit. The abelian forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. Naturality along the canonical isomorphism to the chosen terminal object transports this to terminal evaluation. All remaining factors in globalSectionsUpperStarMap are canonical isomorphisms, so their composite is an isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09ZG (lemma-h0-topological) and 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), with the recorded inverse-image algebraic-structures comparison
